claims.statement: Attention architecture and a greedy-rollout training baseline independently contribute to performance.
Three attention layers use 128-dimensional embeddings, eight heads, 512-unit feed-forward blocks, residuals and batch normalization, without positional encoding.
A context-dependent glimpse and final single-head clipped attention choose feasible nodes; TSP context includes graph, first-node and last-node embeddings.
REINFORCE uses a frozen greedy baseline; replacement requires a one-sided paired t-test on 10000 evaluation instances at alpha 0.05.
Capacity and node-demand state determine masks; split deliveries add remaining demand to keys and values.
OP masks candidate nodes whose visit and return to the depot would exceed the remaining route budget.
The remaining prize controls depot feasibility; SPCTSP retrains the model and updates this state with realized prizes.
Test sets have 10000 instances; inference uses greedy decoding or 1280 samples; timing totals refer to the test set with differing GPU/CPU hardware.
TSP100 AM greedy and sampling results are 8.12/4.53 percent and 7.94/2.26 percent, against reference 7.76.
CVRP100 sampled result 16.23 is compared with LKH3 15.65; those non-TSP gaps need not be certified optimality gaps.
Quality deteriorates away from training sizes; complex feasibility constraints motivate future backtracking rather than a demonstrated universal mask.
SPCTSP is explicitly retrained instead of sharing the deterministic PCTSP model; common hyperparameters do not imply a generalist checkpoint.
The paper directly links the author-maintained attention-learn-to-route repository.
